cards.explanation: The answer is Around Mount Seir. Moses says, “…for many days we wandered around Mount Seir.” Many days around one mountain. You know when you circle the same block three times hunting for a parking spot? That's the kind of lap I'm picturing.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “They will be afraid of you, so you must be very careful.” The text doesn't say why they'll be afraid. I think a whole nation marching through your backyard would make anybody a little nervous.

The word is careful. The LORD says Esau's people will be afraid, “…so you must be very careful.” Right after that He adds, “Do not provoke them…” Think of walking through a stranger's kitchen with a full tray of cookies. Slow steps, friends.

The answer is that God gave Mount Seir to Esau. The LORD says, “…because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.” So none of that land is going to Israel, “…not even a footprint…” Not one footprint's worth! When God hands something to somebody, friends, it's theirs, and that's the end of it.

The answer is that they pay for it in silver. The LORD says, “You are to pay them in silver for the food you eat and the water you drink.” That's His instruction for passing through Seir. I like it, friends. It's a clean way to treat a neighbor.

The word is nothing! Moses says, “The LORD your God has been with you these forty years, and you have lacked nothing.” Forty years of that. I can't keep a cookie jar stocked for forty minutes, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says, “We turned away from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber, and traveled along the road of the Wilderness of Moab.” They don't stay on the Arabah road. They turn onto the road of the Wilderness of Moab.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD gives Moses His reason: “…because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.” Ar was already given to someone else. So the instruction to Israel is to leave the Moabites alone, and driving them out is the opposite of that.

The answer is that God gave Ar to Lot's descendants. The LORD says, “…because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.” Lot is Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5). Same kind of reason as with Esau's land, friends.

The answer is what Israel did in its own land. The note says the descendants of Esau drove out the Horites and settled in their place, “…just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.” So the note lines up Esau's people in Seir with Israel in their own land. I love a little side note that quietly says, 'You're not the only ones, friends.'

The answer is True, and I love this part. The LORD says, “Now arise and cross over the Brook of Zered.” and Moses says, “So we crossed over the Brook of Zered.” Back at Kadesh, Israel was unwilling to go up (Deuteronomy 1:26). Now the command comes and they go.

The answer is thirty-eight years! Moses says it took that long from Kadesh-barnea until they crossed the Brook of Zered. I thought my years stuck in a junk drawer were long. Thirty-eight years is a lot of wandering.

The answer is that that generation's fighting men died. Moses says the trip lasted “…until that entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.” I think this is a heavy verse, so let's take it plainly. The time was counted out until that moment.

The answer is True! When they get close to the Ammonites, the LORD says, “…do not harass them or provoke them…” And He gives His reason: “…for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites.” Notice the pattern, friends. That's Edom, then Moab, and now Ammon, and each time the LORD says the land is already given.
The answer is none! Zero! Not a crumb! The LORD says, “…I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites.” Then He adds, “I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession.”

The answer is that they drove them out and settled there. The passage says the LORD destroyed the Zamzummites from before the Ammonites, “…who drove them out and settled in their place…” So the Ammonites took the land and made a home there. It's the same pattern the note gives for Seir.

The answer is False. The note says He did this for Esau's descendants who lived in Seir, “…when He destroyed the Horites from before them.” Then they drove them out and have lived there to this day. So the LORD's help is right there in the verse.
